items.q1: How do I run multiple AI coding agents with CodeAgentSwarm?
items.a1: Open CodeAgentSwarm and launch Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI, OpenCode, Kimi Code, Grok Build or Cursor Agent side by side. Each agent runs independently, so you can work on different tasks or projects in parallel while seeing every status in one place.
items.q2: How does CodeAgentSwarm handle project-level organization?
items.a2: CodeAgentSwarm keeps each project's agents, task board and conversation history together. You can switch between codebases without losing context or rebuilding your setup.
items.q3: Do I get real-time visibility and live change tracking?
items.a3: Yes. Live diffs show each agent's code changes as they happen. Dynamic agent titles show what Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI, OpenCode, Kimi Code or Grok Build is working on, and file tracking records exactly what changed and when.
items.q4: Does CodeAgentSwarm support notifications for every AI coding agent?
items.a4: Yes. CodeAgentSwarm sends a desktop notification when any agent finishes a task, needs your input or encounters an error.
items.a5: CodeAgentSwarm saves the full conversation history of every supported CLI across sessions. Search any past chat, decision, or code snippet instantly. Session history is fully searchable, so you never lose context or have to repeat explanations.
items.q6: Can I control what my AI CLI agents have access to?
items.a6: Yes. Visual permission settings control the files and actions available to each agent. You can approve sensitive operations while Turbo Mode handles the safe routine ones within the limits you set.
items.q7: Does CodeAgentSwarm support MCP tools and the MCP marketplace?
items.a7: Yes. CodeAgentSwarm includes full MCP integration with a built-in MCP marketplace. Connect any of the seven supported AI CLI agents to GitHub, Notion, Slack, Supabase, Brave Search, Playwright, PostgreSQL and more. MCP tools extend what your agents can do.
items.q8: Does CodeAgentSwarm help prevent context loss in AI CLI agents?
items.a8: Yes. CodeAgentSwarm keeps searchable conversation history across agent sessions, shows each agent's changes in real time and ties every session to its project. Past work stays easy to find and resume.
items.a9: tmux manages windows. CodeAgentSwarm manages agents: task state, notifications when they finish, live diffs, per-project history and configurable permissions. If you just need to split your screen, tmux works fine. If you want to know what each agent is doing and never miss a thing, you need CodeAgentSwarm.
items.q10: Can I run Claude Code and Codex CLI at the same time?
items.a10: Yes. Each agent session is an independent process, so Claude Code and Codex CLI can run at the same time. Pick the agent for each session and run as many as your plan allows.
items.q11: Does CodeAgentSwarm work with Antigravity CLI?
items.a11: Yes. CodeAgentSwarm runs Antigravity CLI (agy), Google's official successor to the retired Gemini CLI, alongside Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Kimi Code, Grok Build and Cursor Agent, with shared notifications, searchable history and live diffs for every agent.
items.q12: Can I mix different AI CLI agents in one swarm?
items.a12: Yes. A single CodeAgentSwarm workspace can run Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI, OpenCode, Kimi Code, Grok Build and Cursor Agent side by side. Use the best agent for each task and supervise all of them from one place.
items.q13: What is an AI CLI agent swarm?
items.a13: An AI CLI agent swarm is several independent AI coding CLI agents (such as Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI, OpenCode, Kimi Code, Grok Build and Cursor Agent) running in parallel in one place, with shared visibility, notifications and history. CodeAgentSwarm is the desktop workspace built to run and supervise that swarm.
items.a14: Yes. CodeAgentSwarm runs OpenCode alongside Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI, Kimi Code, Grok Build and Cursor Agent. Add one or several OpenCode sessions to the same swarm.
items.q15: Does CodeAgentSwarm work with Kimi Code?
items.a15: Yes. Kimi Code CLI by Moonshot is a first-class agent in CodeAgentSwarm, alongside Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI, OpenCode, Grok Build and Cursor Agent. Pick Kimi Code from the launcher like any other agent and it gets the same notifications, searchable conversation history and live diffs. You can run a full swarm of Kimi Code sessions or mix it with the other CLIs.
items.q16: What is an Agentic Development Environment (ADE), and is CodeAgentSwarm one?
items.a16: An Agentic Development Environment is a workspace built around delegating software tasks to AI coding agents, running them in isolated or parallel sessions and reviewing their results. CodeAgentSwarm is an ADE: it lets you direct Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI, OpenCode, Kimi Code, Grok Build and Cursor Agent from one place while keeping tasks, notifications, history and permissions visible.
items.q17: Does CodeAgentSwarm work with Grok Build?
items.a17: Yes. CodeAgentSwarm runs xAI's Grok Build CLI (the grok command) as a first-class agent, so you can supervise several Grok Build agents alongside Claude Code, Codex or any other supported CLI. You install and log into Grok Build yourself, and CodeAgentSwarm adds desktop notifications, live diffs for every agent, searchable history and per-project switching.
items.q18: Does CodeAgentSwarm work with Cursor Agent CLI?
items.a18: Yes. CodeAgentSwarm connects to the official cursor-agent CLI through ACP. It streams text and tool activity, exposes Agent, Plan and Ask modes, handles permissions and cancellation, respects .cursor/mcp.json and enables resume only when the installed Cursor version advertises loadSession support.

items.q2: Do I need subscriptions to every supported agent?
items.a2: No. Use any supported CLI account you already have. Each provider keeps its own plan and usage limits.
items.q3: Can I mix free and paid CLI accounts?

items.q5: What happens when the Beta ends?

items.a6: macOS 12 or later and Windows 10/11 (x64 and ARM64). Linux coming later.

items.q9: Does CodeAgentSwarm support multi-project workflows with Claude Code?
items.a9: Yes. CodeAgentSwarm is built for multi-project work. Each project keeps its own agent sessions, tasks and conversation history, so you can switch codebases without losing context.
